title: Gluten-Free Vanilla Almond Flour Cupcakes
shortDescription: Fluffy gluten free vanilla cupcakes made with almond flour and tapioca starch, ready in about 43 minutes.
description: These gluten free vanilla cupcakes are soft, light, and hold together like a classic bakery cupcake. The trick is balancing almond flour with tapioca starch, which gives lift without any gluten.
ingredients: 1/3 cup melted unsalted butter, cooled slightly
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1 tsp real vanilla extract, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Whisk almond flour, tapioca starch, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl. Break up any clumps.
In a second bowl, beat eggs and sugar for 1 minute until pale and slightly thick.
Add melted butter, milk, and vanilla extract. Whisk until smooth.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix. Stir just until combined, no dry streaks left.
Divide batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until tops spring back and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
For frosting, beat softened butter 2 minutes until smooth and pale.
Add powdered sugar in two batches, beating well after each addition.
Add cream, vanilla extract, and salt. Beat 2 minutes more until light and fluffy.
Pipe or spread frosting on fully cooled cupcakes. Serve or store.
tips: Weigh your almond flour if you can. Too much packs the batter down and cupcakes turn dense.
Tapioca starch is what gives these cupcakes their spring, so do not swap it for more almond flour.
Let eggs and milk sit out 20 minutes before baking. Cold ingredients make the batter seize.
Frost only fully cooled cupcakes, or the frosting will melt and slide off the top.

faq.question: Why use tapioca starch with almond flour in gluten free cupcakes?
faq.answer: Almond flour alone bakes heavy and dense. Tapioca starch adds stretch and lift, so the crumb stays soft and fluffy instead of falling flat.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy free too?
faq.answer: Yes. Swap the milk for unsweetened almond milk and use a dairy free butter stick in both the batter and the frosting.

faq.question: Why did my gluten free cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the pan was opened too early or the batter was overmixed. Keep the oven closed for the first 12 minutes and stir just until combined.

faq.question: Can I use almond meal instead of almond flour?
faq.answer: Fine, blanched almond flour works best here. Almond meal is coarser and grainier, and it makes the cupcakes heavier and less smooth.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove gluten free vanilla can still be soft and springy. Keep the almond flour to tapioca ratio steady and you will get a fluffy result every time.
